claims.text: Variations in chemical short-range order govern mechanical-property differences among single-phase FCC CrMnFeCoNi and its quaternary and ternary subsets by altering dislocation mobility.
Variations in local lattice distortion govern mechanical-property differences among these FCC alloys by altering dislocation mobility.
Increased SRO creates local dislocation pinning and thereby raises yield strength relative to equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi.
Equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi and selected quaternary or ternary derivatives can be prepared as homogeneous, single-phase FCC materials through similar thermomechanical processing.
Selectively reducing or omitting elements within the CrMnFeCoNi family will vary the propensity for chemical SRO while retaining a single FCC phase.
Chemical SRO is accompanied by local lattice distortion in these alloys.
Enhanced SRO produces spatial fluctuations in bonding and local lattice parameters.
Enhanced SRO increases barriers to dislocation glide.
Enhanced SRO increases barriers to dislocation nucleation.
Local ordered regions act as pinning points that hinder dislocation motion.
Alloys with more SRO than equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi will have higher yield and flow stresses.
Alloys with more SRO may have lower ductility because of reduced dislocation mobility.
Alloys with diminished SRO will have lower strength.
Alloys with diminished SRO will have higher ductility.
Equiatomic CrMnFeCoNi has a moderate level of SRO and balanced mechanical properties.
Residual stress and grain-size effects may be convoluted with the strengthening contribution attributed to SRO.
The proposed mechanism is limited to single-phase FCC alloys without significant precipitation or phase separation and with grain-size and processing effects controlled.
